Demobilisation Fleet and Plant Coordinator

We are looking to recruit a Demobilisation Fleet and Plant Coordinator to join our IMS and Quality team.

This is a varied and responsible role coordinating the return, disposal and de-registration of company vehicles, plant and equipment during contract demobilisations. You'll help ensure assets are managed efficiently, legal and contractual requirements are met, costs are controlled and company information is protected throughout the disposal process.

About the Role

Working closely with teams across the business, you'll develop and maintain clear demobilisation and close-out plans covering key activities, responsibilities, deadlines, dependencies and risks.

You'll coordinate with colleagues across operations, commercial, finance, HR, IT, property, procurement, health and safety and environmental functions to support an organised transition. You'll maintain action trackers, risk and issue logs, decision records and progress updates, escalating any potential delays or unresolved issues where required.

You'll review plant and equipment hire agreements to identify notice periods, termination costs and return conditions, while maintaining accurate information covering the location, ownership and status of vehicles, plant and equipment.

You'll also arrange the collection, inspection and return of leased vehicles, ensuring items such as keys, fuel cards, charging equipment and supporting documentation are recovered. Where end-of-contract charges arise, you'll obtain the relevant evidence, challenge discrepancies where appropriate and escalate significant costs in line with the correct approval process.

As part of the de-registration process, you'll coordinate the removal of company branding, dashcams, GPS trackers and telematics equipment, ensuring that company data is removed securely before assets are handed over.

You'll work with the Fleet Manager to update insurance arrangements and reconcile fuel cards, toll accounts, congestion charges, clean-air charging accounts, fines and supplier invoices. You'll maintain a complete audit trail of inspections, returns, disposals, approvals, charges and account closures, ensuring internal and supplier systems remain accurate and up to date.

About You

You'll have previous project management or project coordination experience, with the ability to manage several activities, deadlines and stakeholders at the same time.

Highly organised and confident working with detailed information, you'll have strong data-management skills and be comfortable maintaining plans, trackers, reports and audit records. You'll be able to work effectively within time-sensitive situations, identify emerging risks and make sure outstanding actions are followed through to completion.

Strong people-management and stakeholder-coordination skills will be important, as you'll work with teams across several business areas to deliver an orderly and compliant demobilisation process.

The ability to read and interpret contracts would be advantageous, along with commercial awareness and experience of negotiation, resolving discrepancies or managing supplier disputes.

A full UK manual driving licence, held for a minimum of 12 months, is required.
